title: A Horizon for the Rivergate
premise: Desert ranger Silas Pemberton has spent nine years chasing small crimes across the Rivergate Basin, a borderland of salt flats and monsoon rivers where the government's new concession permits are quietly erasing the nomad routes he grew up on. When a survey team vanishes without tracks, Silas and his reluctant partner, cartographer Wren Oduya, follow the only clue left behind: a stolen compass that points somewhere that shouldn't exist. Their search collides with Naya, a thief whose theft was an act of sabotage against the survey, and together they uncover that the vanished team found evidence the permits were built on falsified maps—evidence someone powerful will flood the basin to destroy. Betrayed by the ranger authority Silas served, hunted through the rising monsoon, the three survive a sinking boat and a drowned canyon to reach the capital with the original maps, exposing the concession scheme at the cost of Silas's badge. In the end, Silas stops running: he chooses the found family who stayed, and a horizon no longer defined by what he's fleeing.
about_author: Paloma Thackeray is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent six years mapping seasonal waterways before turning to fiction full-time. She writes adventure novels about landscapes that outlast the people who try to own them.

chapters.title: Salt and Small Debts
chapters.summary: Silas Pemberton tracks a petty thief across the empty flats, narrating his philosophy that stopping costs more than moving. He catches her—Naya—but she escapes with his water ration and his old service compass. The beat is weary competence masking loneliness; we learn the permits have closed his last legal route home.

chapters.title: The Survey That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Wren Oduya, a government cartographer, hires Silas to find a missing survey team near the drowned canyons. At the campsite: intact gear, cold tea, no tracks, no bodies. Silas's POV; the emotional beat is professional unease curdling into dread as he realizes the absence of tracks is itself impossible—and deliberate.

chapters.title: A Compass That Lies
chapters.summary: Wren discovers the team's instruments were tampered with, their maps replaced with forgeries. Silas recognizes the forgery style—it matches documents tied to the concession office. POV alternates via recovered journal entries from survey leader Ilsa Voss. Beat: the mystery sharpens into conspiracy.

chapters.title: The Thief Who Knew
chapters.summary: Silas corners Naya in a river market, but she reveals she stole the compass because it belonged to her brother, a survey guide who vanished with the team. Reluctant alliance forms. Naya's POV; beat is grief weaponized into purpose, and Silas recognizing a mirror of his own refusal to stop.

chapters.title: Permits and Paper Walls
chapters.summary: In the town of Corren's Landing, Wren pulls permit records and finds the concession boundaries were drawn from maps dated after the land they describe—an impossibility unless forged. Deputy Concessioner Aldous Reeve appears, charming and watchful. Wren's POV; beat: first direct contact with the antagonist's machinery.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Following Naya's brother's route, the trio finds a hidden cache: Ilsa Voss's real maps showing the basin sits atop an aquifer the government secretly knew about. Silas's POV; beat is awe and fear—the land itself is the prize, and they now hold the thing worth killing for.

chapters.title: Riders on the Flats
chapters.summary: Concession enforcers ambush them at dusk. A running fight across the salt; Wren is wounded shielding the maps. They escape by driving their boat into the flooding river channel as the monsoon arrives early. Silas's POV; beat: the chase becomes survival, and the season turns against them.

chapters.title: Leaking Hull, Rising Water
chapters.summary: Trapped on the flooded river with a holed boat, they bail and patch through a brutal night. Naya confesses her brother sent her a warning letter she never opened until it was too late. Naya's POV; beat: guilt surfaces, and the trio's bond hardens from convenience into loyalty.

chapters.title: The Stranger at Drowned Bend
chapters.summary: They wreck near a hermit fisherman, Odell Brack, who owes Silas a debt from years ago and shelters them despite the risk. Odell knows the drowned canyons intimately—and knows where Voss's team went. Odell's POV; beat: kindness as quiet defiance, and the theme of found family taking root.

chapters.title: Into the Drowned Canyon
chapters.summary: Odell guides them upriver into canyons submerged by the new dam works. In a half-flooded cave they find two survivors from the survey team, including Ilsa Voss, starving and hiding. Wren's POV; beat: hope rekindled, but Voss is paranoid, convinced everyone is bought—including Silas.

chapters.title: Voss's Testimony
chapters.summary: Voss reveals the team found the aquifer surveys proving Reeve's permits were fraudulent, and that her own deputy sold them out; the 'vanishing' was her escape plan gone wrong. She entrusts them her sealed testimony. Voss's POV; beat: the weight of truth passed hand to hand like something fragile.

chapters.title: The Badge They Take Back
chapters.summary: Silas contacts his old ranger commander for extraction and instead learns a warrant has been issued for him—Reeve has framed him for the survey team's disappearance. Betrayed by the institution that made him. Silas's POV; beat: identity crisis—he is now officially the criminal he spent his life hunting.

chapters.title: Odell's Price
chapters.summary: Enforcers trace them to Odell's camp. He stays behind to stall them and is taken captive. The trio flees downriver carrying guilt and Voss's testimony. Naya's POV; beat: rage and helplessness—found family means having something to lose.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season
chapters.summary: The storm peaks; the river becomes a brown torrent. They navigate rapids in the patched boat, Wren feverish from her wound, Naya navigating by memory of her brother's letters. Naya's POV; beat: the landscape as antagonist, and trust earned through shared peril.

chapters.title: The Ferry at Last Light
chapters.summary: They reach a ferry crossing held by nomad families the permits displaced. Silas, once the ranger who enforced those permits' edges, asks for help and receives it anyway. Silas's POV; beat: shame met with grace—the people he policed become the family that saves him.

chapters.title: What Reeve Wants
chapters.summary: Interlude: Reeve interrogates Odell, revealing his motive—not just profit, but a belief that order requires someone to own the map entirely. He offers Odell freedom for their location. Reeve's POV; beat: the antagonist humanized and more frightening for it—corruption as sincere conviction.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Weir
chapters.summary: Enforcers trap them at an old weir. In the fight, the boat is destroyed and the maps nearly lost; Wren nearly drowns retrieving them. Silas takes a bullet graze covering her retreat. Wren's POV; beat: sacrifice made explicit—each has now bled for the others.

chapters.title: The Long Road to the Capital
chapters.summary: On foot through flooded lowlands, exhausted, they debate turning back. Voss's testimony could still be dismissed; Reeve owns the courts. Naya proposes going public through the nomad network instead of official channels. Silas's POV; beat: despair transmuted into strategy—stop playing their game.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Maps
chapters.summary: In the capital, the nomads stage a public mapping ceremony, laying Voss's originals beside the concession maps before gathered press and officials. Reeve moves to seize them; Silas publicly surrenders himself to force a hearing. Climax begins; beat: courage as spectacle, truth made undeniable.

chapters.title: Concession Revoked
chapters.summary: Climax: at the hearing, Voss testifies, Odell is produced alive—having escaped—and the forged dates are proven. Reeve, cornered, attempts to destroy the maps and is arrested by rangers who finally believe Silas. Silas's POV; beat: vindication that feels less sweet than expected—the system cost him too much to celebrate.

chapters.title: A Badge Returned, Refused
chapters.summary: Resolution begins: the authority offers Silas his badge and a promotion. He declines, choosing instead to work the basin as an independent guide with Wren and Naya. Voss rebuilds the survey honestly; the nomads' routes are restored to the maps. Beat: identity remade by choice rather than duty.

chapters.title: A Horizon for the Rivergate
chapters.summary: Final chapter: the three launch a repaired boat at monsoon's end, Odell waving from the bank. Silas, who kept moving because stopping cost too much, finally stops—at a camp with people who stayed. Closing image: the river running free toward a horizon that belongs to no one. Beat: peace earned, not granted.
